# Real-ESRGAN x4plus (upscaling model)

Used only by the Windows preview's **Upscale…** image tool, run on the device with the Windows ML runtime that ships with Windows (`Windows.AI.MachineLearning`). Approved by the owner on 2026-10-25 as a pinned local model for C11 (the same model the Mac's Upscale uses); nothing is uploaded and the app never downloads it.

- Model and weights: Real-ESRGAN, Wang et al., "Real-ESRGAN: Training Real-World Blind Super-Resolution with Pure Synthetic Data" (ICCVW 2021). Repository https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN, licence BSD-3-Clause (`LICENSE`, revision `a4abfb2979a7bbff3f69f58f58ae324608821e27`).
- Official checkpoint: https://github.com/xinntao/Real-ESRGAN/releases/download/v0.1.0/RealESRGAN_x4plus.pth, 67,040,989 bytes, SHA-256 `4fa0d38905f75ac06eb49a7951b426670021be3018265fd191d2125df9d682f1` (the same file pinned in the Mac's `ThirdParty/RealESRGAN/UPSTREAM.md`). Only `params_ema` is used.
- Conversion: `Convert/` is a small C# build tool written for Swivel (no Python, PyTorch or ONNX packages). It reads the checkpoint's zip/pickle state dict with a reader that accepts only plain float tensors (contiguous, offset 0, finite) and writes the RRDBNet x4 graph — 64 features, 23 RRDB blocks of three residual dense blocks with growth 32, LeakyReLU 0.2, residual scale 0.2, nearest ×2 upsampling twice — as ONNX IR 6 / opset 11 (Conv, LeakyRelu, Concat, Mul, Add, Resize, Identity). The architecture follows the published network (BasicSR's `RRDBNet`, Apache-2.0); no BasicSR or Real-ESRGAN code is used. Input `image` float 1×3×256×256 RGB in 0–1, output `upscaled` float 1×3×1024×1024 (clamped by the app).
- Output: `realesrgan-x4plus.onnx`, 66,903,262 bytes, SHA-256 `ecf0c6c5b5996958746d654cef8af8180f925d537d65581fbc254904b322ab7f`. The conversion is deterministic; `fetch-model.ps1` / `fetch-model.sh` download the checkpoint into the ignored `build/models/`, convert it and refuse the result unless the SHA-256 matches. The app checks the same size and SHA-256 (compiled into `Swivel.Core/Upscale.cs`) on the bytes it loads.
- Verification on a Mac (development only): `onnx.checker` passes; onnxruntime CPU against PyTorch 2.7 RRDBNet with the same checkpoint on a 256×256 photo tile: maximum difference 0.0014/255, at most 1 level after clamping and rounding.
